text: MLP ARCHITECTURE DEFAULT (same optimizer for all choices; regression, XOR, spiral, tabular when Δ<0.1): score = (#LayerNorm'd blocks) + 1 if residual, MINUS 1 if a NON-residual depth≥4 net's LAST block has no LN (K1061); pick the highest. Ties: on regression ReLU/LeakyReLU > GELU > SiLU, then later last-LN (K1022), then greater depth. Corpus MLP arch-only hits 74/110 (spiral 12/16, tabular 17/32). More-LN beats less-LN 61-11 multivariate, 57-12 univariate, 41-4 tabular Δ<0.1. Overrides: regression deep vs shallow (K1074); spiral residual ≥2 blocks deeper (K1020); shared-SGD regression rectifier vs SiLU (K1039); XOR ≥8 feat. Δ≥0.05 (K1018, K1065); tabular Δ≥0.1 (K1009/K1073).
mechanism: Each unnormalized pre-activation layer shrinks hidden RMS (~0.5x for SiLU/GELU at init), so an under-trained deep stack feeds a weak signal to the head; pre-LN restores unit scale and identity paths keep gradient flow, speeding an under-trained net 2-3x. Predicts the LN advantage shrinks once Δ is large enough to learn the scale (tabular Δ>=0.1 reverses, K1009) and where LN destroys label-relevant norm information (2-D spiral, K1020).

regime.note: tabular only when Δ<0.1; spiral handled by K1020; same optimizer/lr/T

phase: LN-count win rate: multivariate 61-11, univariate 57-12 (lab same-residual more-LN: multivariate at 32768 samples 8/9, ratio 0.38; univariate 37/39), tabular Δ<0.1 41-4 but Δ>=0.1 less-LN 17-6 (K1009); residual at equal LN is the weakest term (lab regression 19/29, ratio ~0.96; q_ca0dea plain beat its residual twin); spiral: K1020; XOR plain+LN vs residual 6/10.

text: Residual × depth × task: on regression, depth helps even without residuals (deeper plain beats shallower residual 24-15) because composed nonlinearities are needed for curvature; on classification, depth WITHOUT residual hurts (shallower residual beats deeper plain 19-13) while deeper residual beats shallower plain 33-14. So for CE tasks never pick a deep (≥4) plain stack over a residual one at the same optimizer; for MSE tasks a deep plain stack with ≥2 LN blocks is still competitive. Deep residual MLPs win 53% of their appearances vs 29% for deep plain.

XOR with ≥8 input features (≥6 noise distractors), same optimizer: the architecture rule FLIPS at shared core-rule Δ≈0.05. Δ≥0.05 (e.g. Adam-family lr·T≥0.05): GELU/SiLU beats ReLU/LeakyReLU (lab 15/16, CE ratio 0.78; corpus 6/6); FEWER LayerNorms win (more-LN wins only 8/32 lab, 5/11 corpus); a ≤2-block net beats one ≥3 blocks deeper (lab 5/5, ratio 0.51; corpus 2/3; q_bfba99, q_e914b6). Δ<0.05 (e.g. SGD m0.9 3e-4×1024): normal rule - more LN wins 33/41 (ratio 0.93), deeper beats shallow (shallow 4/14), activation ~coin flip (smooth 3/8). With <8 features keep deeper (7/7); more-LN there is a coin flip at Δ≥0.05 (4/8). Depth×residual: K1065.
mechanism: With many distractor coordinates and only ~1024 rows, once the XOR interaction is learned (Δ≥0.05) further capacity of deep LN'd stacks is spent fitting distractor-dependent features and sharpening confidence near the axes, raising test CE; a shallow wide smooth net fits the 2-coordinate product with fewer composed nonlinearities. Predicts the reversal vanishes for ≤4 features (no distractors) or Δ<0.05 (boundary not yet learned) — both observed.
phase: nf≥8: Δ≥0.05 smooth 15/16, more-LN 8/32, shallow vs ≥3 deeper 5/5; Δ<0.05 more-LN 33/41, shallow 4/14, smooth 3/8. nf<8: Δ≥0.05 more-LN 4/8, deeper 7/7 corpus + 2/2 lab; Δ<0.05 more-LN 8/11.

text: CLASSIFICATION MLPs (XOR/spiral/tabular), shared optimizer, Δ<0.1: RESIDUAL net vs NON-residual depth≥4 net with MORE LayerNorms — look at the plain net's LAST hidden block. Last block un-normalized → the residual net wins (lab SGD 16/16, CE ratio 0.72; adaptive 5/9; corpus 5/5): LNs followed by an unnormalized tail don't count. Last block LN'd → family-dependent: XOR+SGD plain wins 9/10; spiral+Adam-family plain wins 22/23 (residual CE ×1.3-1.4); spiral+SGD residual wins (lab 3/3, controlled 2/2, ratio 0.3-0.8); tabular ~coin flip (lab 12/27, corpus 6/6 plain). Moving LN to the last block (same count) lowered plain CE in 6/6 controlled cells.
mechanism: An unnormalized final block after LN'd blocks re-shrinks/attenuates features right before the head, so the plain net's earlier LNs buy little; a residual path carries signal past it. Predicts: the effect vanishes once the plain tail is LN'd (observed), and weakens at larger Δ where every net trains (observed at Δ≥0.1).

regime.note: residual net has fewer LN than the deep plain net; same optimizer config for both; Δ>=0.1 mixed (spiral residual 6/13)

phase: plain last-noLN: residual wins 26/30 (lab+corpus). plain last-LN: XOR-SGD plain 9/10; spiral-adaptive plain 22/23; spiral-SGD residual 3/3 (+2/2 controlled); tabular plain 12/27 lab, 6/6 corpus. Δ≥0.1 (adaptive): residual ~50% (spiral 6/13) — rule off.
